entry_conditions: This policy covers the full expanded finish_red slice and may take over partway through the shared transition, not only after a completed blue placement. At inspected earliest states, blue is near its world goal XY but suspended at center z approximately 0.137-0.209 m, red is supported near [-0.181,0,0.020] m in the buffer, TCP is nearly at blue height with about 0.009 m horizontal offset, and each finger is about 0.01825 m (total width about 0.0365 m) while the demonstrated gripper command is -1. These are observed support ranges, not hard rejection thresholds or proof of grasp. Causal input fields are qpos 0:9, qvel 9:18, TCP xyz/wxyz 18:25, red xyz/wxyz 25:32, blue xyz/wxyz 32:39 and goals 41:47, using world metres and joint radians. Two observations expose finger opening/closing and relative object/TCP motion. Blue positive XY margins alone must not be interpreted as completion while its z margin is negative. Later entry during blue opening/retreat or red approach, closure and lift is also within the supplied overlap support.
exit_conditions: Task completion is exactly red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal for one observed state: for each supplied unit wxyz orientation form R, e_x=0.02*sum_j abs(R_xj), e_y=0.02*sum_j abs(R_yj); require 0.06-abs(p_x-g_x)-e_x>=0, 0.06-abs(p_y-g_y)-e_y>=0 and 0.011-abs(p_z-g_z)>=0. Goals are red [-0.35,0.20,0.02] and blue [-0.35,-0.20,0.02] m. Exact observed geometry, not learned mode/support probabilities, is authoritative. Inspected terminals have red near [-0.351,0.195-0.196,0.020] and blue near [-0.350 to -0.3524,-0.201 to -0.199,0.020] m. The demonstrated terminal interface also opens fingers to about 0.040 m each, separates TCP upward to z about 0.300 m and nearly stops qvel. Those are useful continuation cues, not additional task-success requirements; no release, clearance, speed threshold or hold duration is required by the contract.
overlap_role: All supplied overlap actions remain in training. The measured overlaps with transfer_blue are 239-250 actions per trajectory; examples are demo10100 [600,850), demo10111 [603,844) and demo10110 [607,849). This model learns blue descent with closed fingers, setdown/support and opening, vertical retreat, travel toward buffered red, red approach/closure and red lift. In demo10100, blue descends from z=0.2093 at 600 to z=0.0219 at 630; fingers are opening by 640 and TCP reaches z=0.2995 by 700 while blue stays supported. Red is approached by 800 and lifted near z=0.2127 at 850. Thus the shared interval is a learned transition, not an assumption that blue was released before entry. Containment conditioning and per-object supervised future-margin windows apply first to blue and later to red; blue-preservation guidance remains active on supported blue labels during red manipulation. No source-index schedule is used at deployment.
successor_readiness: There is no next manipulation skill in this task. Expose the exact observed conjunction to the task-level evaluator using the one-observation contract. If execution continues for a useful terminal interface, the same learned policy includes demonstrated red release, settling and TCP retreat, leaving both blocks in their respective regions and the hand open and separated. A closed gripper near the placed object is not evidence that release/retreat has finished, even though the task can already be successful. Similarly, the first blue containment observation does not establish completion of its shared opening/retreat transition. TCP/object separation, observed object persistence under hand motion and finger widening distinguish these interfaces; they remain inferred contact cues rather than force measurements.
failure_signatures: Center-only alignment or a high learned probability can miss a rotated corner outside the square; compute full-footprint margins. Red aligned in XY but high is not complete: demo10100:960 has red z=0.05116 m. Blue at entry is also aligned but suspended. If a supposedly released object rises with the hand, release was not achieved; if blue moves out of its region during red retrieval, the preserved-goal assumption has failed. Finger closing without subsequent red/TCP co-motion can indicate a missed grasp, but grasp recovery was not demonstrated or validated. Future-pose predictions may be overconfident and must not replace actual object observations.
continuation_guidance: Use causal geometry and motion to decide invocation duration, not a preset phase length. While blue is suspended, continue the learned descent/open/retreat part rather than assuming red-only execution. With blue supported and red still buffered, continue through red approach, closure and lift; with red moving near the hand, continue learned transfer and setdown while checking blue preservation. If red has positive XY margins but excessive height, placement still needs continuation. Once both exact observed predicates hold, the task evaluator may accept success immediately. If further actions are desired, the learned data support opening and retreat rather than regrasping; demo10111:966 is already successful with command -1, whereas 978 shows opening and 997 shows retreat. There is no implemented deployment stop/hold rule beyond this API guidance. Significant slips, object displacement or states outside the supported transition family should trigger task-level reassessment rather than reliance on an untested recovery claim.
limitations: Observed training starts, ends and overlap examples are evidence, not tests of this policy's success. Successful centered placements with near-identity orientations cannot establish rotated-edge recovery or general collision avoidance. Support labels are height proxies and closed-finger object/TCP co-motion only suggests grasp. The learned outcome model is a local action-conditioned surrogate with no IK, rigid-body simulator or contact sensor. The implementation adapts proposed soft online sampling guidance into masked training-time action-gradient margin losses and causal mode conditioning; it does not rank multiple sampled chunks or enforce hard containment. It uses one complete-demonstration shared normalizer without per-skill refitting. Future observations are labels only, and no trajectory index or noncausal observation enters deployment. Extended terminal holding and recovery from severe disturbances remain unspecified.
